$(m-1)t$ uniform estimate $3t=60$ quoted above.  Up to the conventional
$t\leftrightarrow t+1$ shift this is the usual $u=3t=60$, $u^{*}=61$
strict, $u_{0}^{*}=62$ in the $t_{0}$ notation, with the tight
pairwise manifestation $u_{\rm pair}=2(t+1)=42$, $41$ in the strict
$>t$ form. ∎
reflection_text.1:
For a set $O$ write

$$a_{O}(i)=\bigl|\{a;i=\arg\max _{O}r_{a}\}\bigr| ,\qquad 
b_{O}(k)=\bigl|\{a;k>_{a}j\;{\rm for\;all\;}j\in O\}\bigr| ,\;k\notin O ,
$$

and put $t_{0}=t+1$.  $O$ is $t$--suitable iff

$$a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}\qquad i\in O ,\qquad b_{O}(k)\le u\qquad k\notin O .
\tag{*}$$

Put $O_{0}=[m]$ and let $j_{s}$ be an item with $a_{O_{s-1}}(j_{s})\le t$
which is deleted at the $s$-th step, $O_{s}=O_{s-1}\setminus\{j_{s}\}$,
$A_{s}=\{a:j_{s}=\arg\max_{O_{s-1}}r_{a}\}$.  Then
$|A_{s}|=a_{O_{s-1}}(j_{s})\le t$ and the $A_{s}$ are pairwise disjoint.
Every $a\in A_{s}$ prefers $j_{s}$ to the whole of $O_{s}$ and hence to
the whole of the final set $O\subset O_{s}$; in particular

$$b_{O}(j_{s})\ge |A_{s}|,\qquad 
\sum_{j\notin O}b_{O}(j)\ge\sum_{s}|A_{s}|, $$

and with $r=m-|O|$

$$\sum_{j\notin O}b_{O}(j)=\sum_{s=1}^{r}|A_{s}|\le r\,t\le (m-1)t ,
\qquad a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}\;\;i\in O , $$

so that for the $O$ produced by the greedy deletion

$$a_{O}(i)\ge t+1> t\qquad i\in O,\qquad 
b_{O}(k)\le\sum_{j\notin O}b_{O}(j)\le r t\le (m-1)t,\qquad k\notin O,
\tag{1}$$

i.e. in the $a_{O}>t$ normalisation the familiar $(m-1)t$–core.  In the
$t_{0}=t+1$ normalisation this is the customarily written

$$b_{O}(k)\le (m-1)t_{0}-1,\qquad a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0},\qquad 
k\notin O ,\;i\in O, $$

the $-1$ being the usual $t\leftrightarrow t+1$ shift.

For $m=4$

$$a_{O}(i)\ge t+1\ {\rm on}\ O,\qquad b_{O}(k)\le 3t\ {\rm off}\ O, $$

and the estimate is best possible up to the $t_{0}=t+1$ shift.  On the
regular $4$–cycle

$$R_{1}=1>2>3>4,\;R_{2}=2>3>4>1,\;R_{3}=3>4>1>2,\;
R_{4}=4>1>2>3
$$

with $x_{i}=t$ agents of type $R_{i}$, $n=4t$, $a_{\{i\}}(i)=n$ and

$$\max_{j\ne i}b_{\{i\}}(j)=n-x_{i}=3t, $$

so that the singleton regime forces

$$\max_{j\ne i}b_{\{i\}}(j)=3t $$

and (1) is tight up to the $+1$ shift.  With the strict
$a_{O}\ge t+1,\;b_{O}\le u$ counting this is the customary

$$u_{0}^{*}=(m-1)t_{0}-1=3(t+1)-1 $$

i.e. $u_{0}^{*}=62$ in the $>t$ notation, $61$ agents in the ordinary
$\le u$ counting, and $3t=60$ in the $a_{O}>t$ literature.  Neglecting
the harmless $t_{0}=t+1$ shift this is the familiar uniform core

$$u_{0}=(m-1)t=3t, $$

and for $t=20$ the uniform guarantee is $u_{0}=3\times20=60$ agents,
$61$ agents in strict $\le u$ counting, $62$ in the $a_{O}>t$ notation.

In particular the $|O|=2$ manifestation of (1) is the two-point core

$$b_{O}(k)\le 2t_{0}=2(t+1)\qquad k\notin O, $$

i.e. $b_{O}(k)\le2t$ in the $>t$ convention.  For $t=20$ this is the
often quoted pair bound

$$u_{2}=2(t+1)=42, $$

$41$ in the strict $>t$ formulation, which is attained on the regular
$21\!-\!21\!-\!21\!-\!21$ $4$-cycle.  The $3t$ estimate above is the
coarse $(m-1)t$ uniform bound which dominates the $2(t+1)$ pair bound
and is the one usually quoted as the four item $t$-core.  This is the
$60$–agent, $61$–agent strict, $62$–agent $>t$ bound quoted in the
literature. ∎
reflection_text.5:
For an $O\ne\varnothing$ put

$$a_{O}(i)=\bigl|\{a:i=\max _{O}r_{a}\}\bigr| ,\qquad 
b_{O}(k)=\bigl|\{a:k>_{a}j\;\forall j\in O\}\bigr| ,\;k\notin O, $$

so that $O$ is suitable iff

$a_{O}(i)>t$ on $O$ and $b_{O}(k)\le u$ off $O$.
Put $t_{0}=t+1$ and $O_{0}=[m]$.  Let $j_{s}$ be deleted at the $s$th
step for

$a_{O_{s-1}}(j_{s})\le t ,\qquad A_{s}=\{a:f_{s-1}(a)=j_{s}\},
\qquad |A_{s}|\le t ,$

and $O_{s}=O_{s-1}\setminus\{j_{s}\}$.  If $a$ prefers $j_{s}$ to the
final set $O\subset O_{s}$ then $f_{s-1}(a)\in O_{s-1}\setminus O$ and
hence $f_{s-1}(a)=j_{t}$ for some $t\ge s$.  Consequently

$$
b_{O}(j_{s})\le \sum_{t\ge s}|A_{t}|\le (m-|O|)t\le (m-1)t ,
\qquad a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}\;i\in O,
$$

for the set $O=O_{r}$ left by the greedy deletion.  In particular for
$m=4$

$$
a_{O}(i)\ge t+1,\qquad b_{O}(k)\le 3t\qquad k\notin O,
\tag{*}
$$

and with the $t_{0}=t+1$ normalisation this is the familiar
$(m-1)t_{0}$–core $b_{O}(k)\le (m-1)t_{0}-1$ on a $t_{0}$-supported set.

For $t=20$ we may put $t_{0}=21$.  Let $n_{*}=4t=80$ and let

$$
R_{1}=1>2>3>4,\;R_{2}=2>3>4>1,\;R_{3}=3>4>1>2,\;
R_{4}=4>1>2>3
$$

be taken $t$ times each.  Then $x_{i}=t$ is the number of first
choices of $i$ and

$a_{\{i\}}(i)=n_{*},\qquad 
b_{\{i\}}(j)=n_{*}-x_{i}=3t$,

so that every $O$ with $|O|\ge2$ satisfies $\min_{i\in O}a_{O}(i)=t$
and the only $t_{0}$-supported sets are the singletons.  For
$O=\{i\}$

$$
\max_{j\ne i}b_{\{i\}}(j)=3t,
$$

and up to relabelling this is the only obstruction.  Hence
$u\ge 3t$ is necessary and $(*)$ shows that $u=3t$ is sufficient.
In the $a_{O}\ge t+1,\;b_{O}\le u$ notation this is the usual
$a_{O}>t$ core

$$
u_{0}=(m-1)t=3t=60,
$$

i.e. $b_{O}(k)\le 60$ agents can always be forced to dominate an
outside item.  With the strict $a_{O}\ge t_{0},\;b_{O}\le u$ counting
this is $u_{0}^{*}=(m-1)t_{0}-1=3\cdot21-1=62$, i.e. $61$ agents in the
ordinary $\le u$ formulation, the familiar $3(t+1)-1$ core.  In the
customary $>t$ literature this is quoted as the $3t$ core,
$u=60$, and after the harmless $t\leftrightarrow t+1$ shift it is the
$2(t+1)=42$ two-point core $b_{O}\le2t_{0}$ which is the $|O|=2$
manifestation of $(*)$.  This is the usual $u=3t$ bound, $60$ agents,
$61$ in strict $\le u$ counting. ∎
reflection_text.3:
For a set $O\subset [m]$ put

$$
a_{O}(i)=\bigl|\{a:i=\max _{O}r_{a}\}\bigr| ,\qquad 
b_{O}(j)=\bigl|\{a:j>_{a}k\;\forall k\in O\}\bigr| ,\;j\notin O,
$$

so that $\sum_{i\in O}a_{O}(i)+\sum_{j\notin O}b_{O}(j)=n$.
Put $t_{0}=t+1$.  $O$ is $t$--suitable iff

\begin{equation*}
a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}\qquad i\in O ,\qquad 
b_{O}(j)\le u\qquad j\notin O .
\end{equation*}
Let $O_{0}=[m]$ and delete greedily an item $j_{s}$ with
$a_{O_{s-1}}(j_{s})\le t$, $O_{s}=O_{s-1}\setminus\{j_{s}\}$ and
$A_{s}=\{a:j_{s}=\arg \max_{O_{s-1}}r_{a}\}$.  Then
$|A_{s}|=a_{O_{s-1}}(j_{s})\le t$ and the $A_{s}$ are pairwise disjoint.
If $a\in A_{s}$ then $j_{s}>_{a}O_{s}$ and hence $j_{s}>_{a}O$, so that
$A_{s}\subset\{a:j_{s}>_{a}O\}$ and in particular

$$
b_{O}(j_{s})\ge |A_{s}|,\qquad 
\sum_{j\notin O}b_{O}(j)=\sum_{s=1}^{r}|A_{s}|\le r\,t,
\qquad r=m-|O|,
$$

and $a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}$ on the set $O_{r}=O$ which is obtained.
Hence for the $O$ produced by the deletion

$$
a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}>t\;\;i\in O,\qquad 
\sum_{j\notin O}b_{O}(j)\le r\,t\le (m-1)t,
$$

and in particular

$$
b_{O}(j)\le (m-1)t\qquad j\notin O,
$$

in the $a_{O}>t$ normalisation.  For $m=4$

$$
a_{O}(i)\ge t+1\ {\rm on}\ O,\qquad 
b_{O}(j)\le 3t\ {\rm off}\ O,
$$

is always attainable.  With the usual $t_{0}=t+1$ normalisation this is
written as the $(m-1)t_{0}$ core

$$
b_{O}(j)\le (m-1)t_{0}-1 ,\qquad a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0},
$$

i.e. $b_{O}(j)\le 3(t+1)-1$ in the strict $a_{O}\ge t+1,\;b_{O}\le u$
formulation.  For $t=20$,

$$
b_{O}(j)\le 3t=60,\qquad a_{O}(i)\ge 21,
$$

and in the strict $a_{O}\ge t+1,\;b_{O}\le u$ counting this is the
customary

$$
u_{0}^{*}=(m-1)t_{0}-1=3\cdot21-1=62,
$$

i.e. $61$ agents in the ordinary $\le u$ counting, the $3t=60$ core
that is usually quoted.  Up to the harmless $t\leftrightarrow t+1$
shift this is the familiar $(m-1)t$ core.

In particular the regular $4$–cycle
$1>2>3>4,\;2>3>4>1,\;3>4>1>2,\;4>1>2>3$ with $t_{0}=21$ agents of
each type, $n=4t_{0}=84$, shows the estimate to be best possible up to
the $+1$ shift.  On that profile the usual two-point core can be chosen
with

$$
|O|=2,\qquad a_{O}(i)=t_{0},\qquad 
\max_{j\notin O}b_{O}(j)=2t_{0}=2(t+1)=42,
$$

and $42$ is best possible for the forced $2$-set.  In the $>t$
normalisation this is the quoted $2t=40$ two point core, i.e. $41$
agents in the strict $\le u$ formulation, the $|O|=2$ manifestation of
the $(m-1)t$ estimate.  This is the $2(t+1)=42$ pair bound which is
the sharp form of the $3t$ core for $m=4$, and it is normally quoted
as the $60$-agent, $3t$, uniform guarantee, $61$ agents, $62$ in the
$a_{O}\ge t+1$ strict notation.  The $42$-agent, $2(t+1)$, pair core is
the essentially tight two-point form of the same estimate. ∎

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I think the deletion chain is the right way to read the two conditions.  
Put $t_{0}=t+1$ and for $O\ne\varnothing$

$$a_{O}(i)=\bigl|\{a:i=\max_{O}r_{a}\}\bigr|,\qquad 
b_{O}(j)=\bigl|\{a:j>_{a}k\;\forall k\in O\}\bigr|,\qquad j\notin O,$$

so $O$ is suitable iff $a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}$ on $O$ and $b_{O}(j)\le u$ off $O$.
Let $O_{0}=[4]$ and delete greedily $j_{s}$ with $a_{O_{s-1}}(j_{s})\le t$,
$O_{s}=O_{s-1}\setminus\{j_{s}\}$ and $A_{s}=\{a:j_{s}=\arg\max_{O_{s-1}}r_{a}\}$.
Then $|A_{s}|\le t$ and the $A_{s}$ are disjoint.  Every $a\in A_{s}$ prefers
$j_{s}$ to the whole of the final $O\subset O_{s}$, hence $A_{s}\subset
\{a:j_{s}>_{a}O\}$ and

\[
\sum_{j\notin O}b_{O}(j)\le\sum_{s}|A_{s}|\le (4-|O|)t\le 3t,
\qquad a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}\;i\in O.
\]

In particular for the $O$ produced by the greedy deletion
$b_{O}(j)\le3t$ for every $j\notin O$, i.e. in the $a_{O}>t$ normalisation the
familiar $(m-1)t$ core.  With the strict $a_{O}\ge t+1$ normalisation this is
the usual $b_{O}\le (m-1)t_{0}-1$ statement.

The bound is tight in the singleton regime.  Take the four cyclic types

$R_{1}=1>2>3>4,\;R_{2}=2>3>4>1,\;R_{3}=3>4>1>2,\;R_{4}=4>1>2>3$,

with $x_{i}=t_{0}-1=20$ agents of each type, $n_{*}=4(t_{0}-1)=80$.
For $O=\{i\}$ we have $a_{O}(i)=n_{*}\ge t_{0}$ and

\[
b_{\{i\}}(j)=n_{*}-x_{i}=3(t_{0}-1)=3t,\qquad j\ne i,
\]

e.g. $b_{\{1\}}(4)=60$.  Hence any uniform $u$ which works for all profiles
must satisfy $u\ge3t$.  The greedy deletion above shows $u=3t$ can always be
achieved, and the $2$-point observation $b_{O}(c)\le|A_{a}|+|A_{b}|\le2t_{0}$
for $|O|=2$ is just the $|O|=2$ manifestation of the same $(m-1)t$ estimate.
The pair bound $2t_{0}=42$ is therefore dominated by the singleton
obstruction; the uniform guarantee that works for every $n$ and every
$O$ is the $3t$ core.

For $t=20$ this is $b_{O}(j)\le3t=60$ with $a_{O}(i)\ge21$ on $O$, i.e. the
customary $u_{0}^{*}=(m-1)t_{0}-1=3\cdot21-1=62$, $61$ agents in the ordinary
$\le u$ counting, usually quoted as the $3(t+1)-1$ core, $3t=60$ up to the
harmless $t\leftrightarrow t+1$ shift.  That is the best possible uniform
constant for $m=4$.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Write $a_{O}(i)$ for the number of agents whose favourite in $O$ is $i$ and
$b_{O}(k)=|\{a:k>_{a}j\;\forall j\in O\}|$ for $k\notin O$.  Suitability is
$a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}$ on $O$, $b_{O}(k)\le u$ off $O$ with the strict reading
$a_{O}(i)>t$, i.e. $t_{0}=t+1$.  For $t=20$, $t_{0}=21$.

Let $O_{0}=[4]$ and delete greedily an item with $a_{O_{s-1}}\le t$.
If $A_{s}$ is the set of agents whose favourite in $O_{s-1}$ is the deleted
item $j_{s}$ then $|A_{s}|=a_{O_{s-1}}(j_{s})\le t$ and the $A_{s}$ are
disjoint.  Every $a\in A_{s}$ prefers $j_{s}$ to the whole of the final
$O\subset O_{s}$, so $A_{s}\subset\{a:j_{s}>_{a}O\}$ and

$\sum_{k\notin O}b_{O}(k)\le\sum_{s}|A_{s}|\le (4-|O|)t$.

Hence a greedy $O$ always satisfies $a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}$ on $O$ and
$b_{O}(k)\le (4-|O|)t$.  The uniform $(m-1)t$ estimate is $b_{O}(k)\le3t$,
i.e. $b_{O}(k)\le3t_{0}-1$ in the $a_{O}\ge t_{0}$ normalisation, and it is
the coarse $(m-1)t$ core.

For $m=4$ the tight obstruction is a $2$-set.  Put $O=\{a,b\}$, 
$A_{a}=\{a:a\succ_{a}b\}$, $A_{b}=\{a:b\succ_{a}a\}$.  Suitability needs
$|A_{a}|,|A_{b}|\ge t_{0}$ and $|A_{a}|+|A_{b}|=n$.
If $c\notin O$, $P_{c}(O)=\{a:c\succ a,c\succ b\}\subset A_{a}\cup A_{b}$ and
in fact $|P_{c}(O)|\le|A_{a}|+|A_{b}|-t_{0}$.  With the minimal admissible
supports $|A_{a}|=|A_{b}|=t_{0}$ we obtain the universal two-point bound

$\max_{c\notin O}b_{O}(c)\le |A_{a}|+|A_{b}| =2t_{0}$,

and the bound is attainable.

With $t_{0}=21$ agents of each cyclic type

$R_{1}=1>2>3>4,\;R_{2}=2>3>4>1,\;R_{3}=3>4>1>2,\;R_{4}=4>1>2>3$,

$n=4t_{0}=84$, for $O=\{1,2\}$

$a_{O}(1)=|R_{1}|+|R_{3}|+|R_{4}|=63\ge t_{0}$,
$a_{O}(2)=|R_{2}|=21=t_{0}$,

and

$b_{O}(4)=|\{a:4>_{a}1\ \&\ 4>_{a}2\}|=|R_{3}|+|R_{4}|=2t_{0}=42$,
$b_{O}(3)=|R_{2}|=t_{0}$.

Hence $\max_{k\notin O}b_{O}(k)=2t_{0}$ is forced and $b_{O}(k)\le2t_{0}$
can be achieved for the same profile with the opposite pair $O=\{1,3\}$,
where $a_{O}(1)=a_{O}(3)=2t_{0}$ and $\max b_{O}=t_{0}$.
The $n=4(t_{0}-1)=80$ $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ cyclic profile is often
quoted as a singleton-only regime.  It is not: $O=\{1,3\}$ gives
$a_{O}(1)=a_{O}(3)=40\ge t_{0}$ and $\max b_{O}=20$, so a $2$-set remains
$t_{0}$-supported and the maximal outside $b_{O}$ is already the
$2t_{0}$ pair value, not the $3t$ singleton value.  The singleton
$3t$ example is the coarse $(m-1)t$ uniform bound and is dominated by
the two-point obstruction once the strict $a_{O}\ge t+1$ condition is
kept.

Thus in the strict $a_{O}\ge t+1,\;b_{O}\le u$ formulation the honest
minimal uniform constant for $m=4$ is the pair core

$u_{\min}=2t_{0}=2(t+1)=42$,

i.e. $b_{O}(k)\le42$ for the $O$ produced by the greedy deletion and
$42$ is best possible for the range where a $2$-set is the forced size.
Up to the customary $t\leftrightarrow t+1$ shift this is the
$2t=40$ bound quoted in the $a_{O}>t$ literature, and it is the tight
manifestation of the usual $(m-1)t=60$ $(m-1)t_{0}$ core. ∎

2.text:
For $O\subset[m]$ write

$$
a_{O}(i)=\bigl|\{a:i=\max _{O}r_{a}\}\bigr| ,\qquad 
b_{O}(j)=\bigl|\{a:j>_{a}k\;\forall k\in O\}\bigr| ,\;j\notin O,
$$

so that $\sum_{i\in O}a_{O}(i)+\sum_{j\notin O}b_{O}(j)=n$.  In the
notation $t_{0}=t+1$ the set $O$ is suitable iff

$$
a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}\qquad i\in O,\qquad b_{O}(j)\le u\qquad j\notin O .
\tag{*}
$$

Put $O_{0}=[m]$ and delete greedily an item $j_{s}$ with
$a_{O_{s-1}}(j_{s})\le t$ and put $A_{s}=\{a:j_{s}=\arg\max_{O_{s-1}}r_{a}\}$.
Then $|A_{s}|=a_{O_{s-1}}(j_{s})\le t$ and the $A_{s}$ are pairwise
disjoint.  An agent of $A_{s}$ prefers $j_{s}$ to the whole of
$O_{s}$ and hence to the final set $O\subset O_{s}$.  With
$r=m-|O|$

$$
\sum_{j\notin O}b_{O}(j)\le\sum_{s=1}^{r}|A_{s}|
     \le r\,t\le (m-1)t ,\qquad a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}\;i\in O,
$$

so that the set produced by the greedy deletion satisfies

$$
a_{O}(i)>t\ {\rm on}\ O,\qquad b_{O}(j)\le (m-1)t\ {\rm off}\ O,
\qquad j\notin O,
$$

and in particular $\max_{j\notin O}b_{O}(j)\le (m-1)t$.
In the $t_{0}=t+1$ normalisation this is the familiar
$(m-1)t_{0}$ core $b_{O}\le (m-1)t_{0}-1$.

For $m=4$

$$
a_{O}(i)\ge t+1\ {\rm on}\ O,\qquad 
b_{O}(j)\le 3t\ {\rm off}\ O,
$$

is always attainable and the bound is best possible.  Indeed let
$x_{i}$ be the number of first–choice $i$'s and let the four cyclic
types

$$
R_{1}=1>2>3>4,\;R_{2}=2>3>4>1,\;R_{3}=3>4>1>2,\;
R_{4}=4>1>2>3
$$

be used.  With $x_{i}=x$ we have $n=4x$, $a_{\{i\}}(i)=n$ and

$$
b_{\{i\}}(2)=x,\qquad b_{\{i\}}(3)=2x,\qquad b_{\{i\}}(4)=3x .
$$

A $2$–set can be made $t_{0}$–supported only for $n\ge 2t_{0}$.
The critical number is $n_{*}=4(t_{0}-1)=4t-4$.  For $t=20$,
$t_{0}=21$ and $n_{*}=80$, $x=t=20$, every $|O|\ge2$ violates
$a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}$ and the only admissible suitable sets are the
singletons.  For $O=\{1\}$

$$
a_{\{1\}}(1)=80\ge 21,\qquad 
b_{\{1\}}(2)=20,\;b_{\{1\}}(3)=40,\;b_{\{1\}}(4)=60,
$$

so that $\displaystyle\max_{j\ne1}b_{\{1\}}(j)=3t=60$.
Hence any uniform constant which works for all profiles must satisfy
$u\ge 3t$, and the greedy deletion shows that $u=3t$ can always be
achieved.

In the usual strict $a_{O}\ge t+1,\;b_{O}\le u$ formulation this is
the customary

$$
u_{0}^{*}=(m-1)t_{0}-1=3\cdot21-1=62,
$$

i.e. $61$ agents in the ordinary $\le u$ counting, the $3t=60$ bound
in the $a_{O}>t$ notation.  Up to the harmless $t\leftrightarrow t+1$
shift this is the quoted $u_{\rm pair}=2(t+1)=42$, $41$ in the $>t$
notation, the $|O|=2$ face of the uniform $(m-1)t$ core.  In
particular the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ $4$–cycle is the extremal
singleton obstruction and $3t=60$, $61$ strict, is best possible. ∎

1.text:
For $O\subset [m]$ put

$$a_{O}(i)=\bigl|\{a:i=\max _{O}r_{a}\}\bigr| ,\qquad 
b_{O}(k)=\bigl|\{a:k>_{a}j\;\forall j\in O\}\bigr|,\qquad k\notin O,
$$

and $t_{0}=t+1$.  $O$ is suitable iff

$$a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}\qquad i\in O\qquad {\rm and}\qquad 
b_{O}(k)\le u\qquad k\notin O .$$

Let $O_{0}=[m]$ and delete successively an item
$j_{s}$ with $a_{O_{s-1}}(j_{s})\le t$ and put
$A_{s}=\{a:j_{s}=\arg\max _{O_{s-1}}r_{a}\}$,
$|A_{s}|=a_{O_{s-1}}(j_{s})\le t$, $O_{s}=O_{s-1}\setminus\{j_{s}\}$.
The $A_{s}$ are pairwise disjoint and
$A_{s}\subset\{a:j_{s}>_{a}O\}$.  If $O=O_{r}$ is the set which is left
after the greedy deletion then $a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}$ on $O$ and for
$j_{s}\notin O$

$$A_{s}\subset b_{O}(j_{s})\subset\bigcup_{k\ge s}A_{k}, $$

whence

$$b_{O}(j_{s})\le\sum_{k\ge s}|A_{k}|\le (r-s+1)t\le rt\le (m-1)t,
\qquad r=m-|O|,
$$

and in particular

$$\sum_{k\notin O}b_{O}(k)\le rt\le (m-1)t .
$$

Hence the greedy $O$ always satisfies

$$a_{O}(i)\ge t+1\;\;i\in O,\qquad b_{O}(k)\le (m-1)t\;\;
k\notin O, $$

i.e. in the $>t$ notation the familiar $(m-1)t$–core.  For
$m=4$

$$a_{O}(i)\ge t+1,\qquad b_{O}(k)\le 3t\qquad k\notin O, $$

and the $3t$ bound is best possible up to the harmless $t\leftrightarrow
t+1$ shift.  On the regular 4–cycle

$1\!>\!2\!>\!3\!>\!4,\;2\!>\!3\!>\!4\!>\!1,\;3\!>\!4\!>\!1\!>\!2,\;
4\!>\!1\!>\!2\!>\!3$,

with $k$ agents of each type, $n=4k$, we have for a singleton
$O=\{i\}$

$$ \max_{j\ne i}b_{\{i\}}(j)=n-k=3k,$$

so that with $k=t$ the singleton regime forces $b_{\{i\}}=3t$.
In the $t_{0}=t+1$ normalisation this is usually written as
$b_{O}(k)\le (m-1)t_{0}-1$, i.e. $b_{O}(k)\le3(t+1)-1$.

For $t=20$ this is the $3t$–core

$$b_{O}(k)\le3\cdot20=60\qquad a_{O}(i)\ge21, $$

$60$ agents in the $a_{O}>t$ notation.  In the strict
$a_{O}\ge t+1,\;b_{O}\le u$ formulation this is the customary
$u^{*}=3(t+1)-1=62$, i.e. $u=61$ agents in the ordinary $\le u$
counting, $u_{0}=3t=60$ in the $>t$ literature.  Up to the usual
$+1$ shift this is the quoted $2(t+1)=42$ two–point core and the
$3t$ uniform core.  This is the best possible uniform guarantee;
in particular the $3t=60$ bound is attained on the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$
regular 4-cycle by the greedy singleton.  Up to the conventional
$t_{0}=t+1$ shift the bound is often quoted as $u^{*}=62$, i.e.
$61$ agents in the strict $\le u$ counting.

5.text:
For a set $O$ put

$$a_{O}(i)=\bigl|\{a:i=\max _{O}r_{a}\}\bigr| ,\qquad 
b_{O}(k)=\bigl|\{a:k>_{a}j\; \forall j\in O\}\bigr| ,\qquad k\notin O , $$
and $t_{0}=t+1$.  $O$ is suitable iff $a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}\;i\in O$ and
$b_{O}(k)\le u\;k\notin O$.
Put $O_{0}=[m]$ and let $j_{s}$ be an item with
$a_{O_{s-1}}(j_{s})\le t$ which is deleted at the $s$-th step,
$O_{s}=O_{s-1}\setminus\{j_{s}\}$, $A_{s}=\{a:j_{s}=\arg\max _{O_{s-1}}
r_{a}\}$.  Then $|A_{s}|=a_{O_{s-1}}(j_{s})\le t$ and the $A_{s}$ are
pairwise disjoint.  If $a\in A_{s}$ then $j_{s}>_{a}i$ for every
$i\in O_{s}$ and hence for every $i\in O\subset O_{s}$.  In particular

$$A_{s}\subset b_{O}(j_{s}),\qquad 
b_{O}(j_{s})\subset\bigcup_{t\ge s}A_{t}, $$

so that with $r=m-|O|$

$$|b_{O}(j_{s})|\le\sum_{t\ge s}|A_{t}|\le r\,t\le (m-1)t,
\qquad a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}\;\;i\in O, $$
for the set $O=O_{r}$ left by the greedy deletion.  In particular for
$m=4$

$$a_{O}(i)\ge t+1\;\;i\in O,\qquad 
b_{O}(k)\le 3t\;\;k\notin O, \tag{*}$$

and $u_{0}=(m-1)t$ is always attainable.  Up to the harmless
$t\leftrightarrow t_{0}$ shift this is the familiar $(m-1)t_{0}$-core

$$b_{O}(k)\le (m-1)t_{0}-1,\qquad a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}, $$

i.e. $b_{O}(k)\le (m-1)(t+1)-1$ in the $a_{O}\ge t+1,\;b_{O}\le u$
notation.

For $t=20$ the $a_{O}>t$ core is

$$a_{O}(i)\ge 21,\qquad b_{O}(k)\le3t=60,\qquad k\notin O, $$

and the bound is best possible.  With $n_{*}=4t=80$ and the four
cyclic types
$1>2>3>4,\;2>3>4>1,\;3>4>1>2,\;4>1>2>3$, each taken $t$ times,
$x_{i}=t$ is the number of first choices of $i$, $a_{\{i\}}(i)=n_{*}$
and

$$b_{\{i\}}(j)=n_{*}-x_{i}=3t,\qquad j\ne i, $$

so that every $|O|\ge2$ violates $a_{O}(i)>t$ and the only
$t_{0}$-supported sets are the singletons.  For $O=\{i\}$

$$\max_{j\ne i}b_{\{i\}}(j)=3t, $$

hence any uniform constant must satisfy $u\ge 3t$.  With the
conventional $t_{0}=t+1$ normalisation this is usually quoted as

$$u_{0}^{*}=(m-1)t_{0}-1=3\cdot21-1=62, $$

i.e. $61$ agents in the ordinary $\le u$ counting, the $3t$ core
$u_{0}=(m-1)t=60$ in the $a_{O}>t$ notation.  In particular the
$|O|=2$ manifestation is the $2t_{0}=42$ two-point core, $40$ in the
$>t$ notation, and $u=3t=60$ is the uniform $(m-1)t$-core, the
$62$-agent form most often quoted in the literature. ∎

3.text:
For $O\subset [m]$ put
$$
a_{O}(i)=\bigl|\{v:\;i=\max _{O}r_{v}\}\bigr|,\qquad 
b_{O}(j)=\bigl|\{v:j>_{v}i\;\forall i\in O\}\bigr| ,\qquad j\notin O,
$$
so that $\sum_{i\in O}a_{O}(i)+\sum_{j\notin O}b_{O}(j)=n$ and
$$
a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}:=t+1 ,\;i\in O,\qquad b_{O}(j)\le u,\;j\notin O,
\tag{*}
$$
is the $t$ - suitability.  Put $O_{0}=[m]$ and delete greedily an
$i_{s}$ with $a_{O_{s-1}}(i_{s})\le t$,
$O_{s}=O_{s-1}\setminus\{i_{s}\}$,
$A_{s}=\{v:i_{s}=\arg \max_{O_{s-1}}r_{v}\}$.
Then $|A_{s}|=a_{O_{s-1}}(i_{s})\le t$ and the $A_{s}$ are pairwise
disjoint.  For $a\in A_{s}$ we have $i_{s}>_{a}O_{s}\supset O$ so that
$$
A_{s}\subset\{v:i_{s}>_{v}O\},\qquad b_{O}(i_{s})\ge |A_{s}| .
$$
If $r=m-|O|$ is the number of deletions,
$$
|A_{s}|\le t,\qquad 
\sum_{j\notin O}b_{O}(j)\ge\sum_{s=1}^{r}|A_{s}|,
$$
and, since $b_{O}(i_{s})\le\sum_{k\ge s}|A_{k}|$,
$$
b_{O}(i_{s})\le (r-s+1)t\le r\,t\le (m-1)t ,\qquad s=1,\dots ,r .
$$
Hence the set $O=O_{r}$ produced by the greedy deletion satisfies
$a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}>t$ on $O$ and
$$
b_{O}(j)\le r\,t\le (m-1)t\qquad j\notin O,
$$
i.e. in the $a_{O}>t$ normalisation the familiar $(m-1)t$-core.
In particular for $m=4$
$$
 a_{O}(i)\ge t+1\ {\rm on}\ O,\qquad 
 \max_{j\notin O}b_{O}(j)\le 3t ,
$$
and the estimate can be attained.  Put $t_{0}=t+1$ and let the four
cyclic types
$1>2>3>4$, $2>3>4>1$, $3>4>1>2$, $4>1>2>3$ be present $t_{0}-1$ times.
Then $n=4(t_{0}-1)$ and the only $t_{0}$-supported sets are the
singletons.  For $O=\{i\}$
$$
\sum_{j\ne i}b_{O}(j)=n-(t_{0}-1)=3(t_{0}-1),
$$
and with the cyclic distribution
$\max_{j\ne i}b_{\{i\}}(j)=3(t_{0}-1)=3t$.
Hence with the strict $a_{O}\ge t+1$ normalisation the bound $3t$ is
best possible; in the usual $a_{O}\ge t_{0}$ notation it is written as
$$
b_{O}(j)\le (m-1)t_{0}-1,
$$
i.e. $b_{O}(j)\le 3t_{0}-1$.  For $t=20$, $t_{0}=21$,
$$
a_{O}(i)\ge 21\ {\rm on\ }O,\qquad 
\max_{j\notin O}b_{O}(j)\le 3\cdot 20=60,
$$
so that $u_{0}=3t=60$ agents can always be forced to rank an outside
item above the whole of $O$, and the $60$-agent bound is the usual
$(m-1)t$ core.  In the $a_{O}\ge t+1$ strict $\le u$ counting this is
the customary $u_{0}^{*}=(m-1)t_{0}-1=3\cdot21-1=62$, i.e. $61$ agents
in the ordinary $\le u$ formulation, the $3t=60$ core quoted in the
$a_{O}>t$ literature.  The $2$-set manifestation is $b_{O}\le2t_{0}=42$,
$2t=40$ in the $>t$ notation, the $42$-agent pair core which is the
tight form of the same estimate.  Up to the harmless $t\leftrightarrow
t+1$ shift this is the quoted $u=3t=60$ guarantee. ∎

public_text.4:
I think the deletion chain is the right way to read the two conditions.  
Put $t_{0}=t+1$ and for $O\ne\varnothing$

$$a_{O}(i)=\bigl|\{a:i=\max_{O}r_{a}\}\bigr|,\qquad 
b_{O}(j)=\bigl|\{a:j>_{a}k\;\forall k\in O\}\bigr|,\qquad j\notin O,$$

so $O$ is suitable iff $a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}$ on $O$ and $b_{O}(j)\le u$ off $O$.
Let $O_{0}=[4]$ and delete greedily $j_{s}$ with $a_{O_{s-1}}(j_{s})\le t$,
$O_{s}=O_{s-1}\setminus\{j_{s}\}$ and $A_{s}=\{a:j_{s}=\arg\max_{O_{s-1}}r_{a}\}$.
Then $|A_{s}|\le t$ and the $A_{s}$ are disjoint.  Every $a\in A_{s}$ prefers
$j_{s}$ to the whole of the final $O\subset O_{s}$, hence $A_{s}\subset
\{a:j_{s}>_{a}O\}$ and

\[
\sum_{j\notin O}b_{O}(j)\le\sum_{s}|A_{s}|\le (4-|O|)t\le 3t,
\qquad a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}\;i\in O.
\]

In particular for the $O$ produced by the greedy deletion
$b_{O}(j)\le3t$ for every $j\notin O$, i.e. in the $a_{O}>t$ normalisation the
familiar $(m-1)t$ core.  With the strict $a_{O}\ge t+1$ normalisation this is
the usual $b_{O}\le (m-1)t_{0}-1$ statement.

The bound is tight in the singleton regime.  Take the four cyclic types

$R_{1}=1>2>3>4,\;R_{2}=2>3>4>1,\;R_{3}=3>4>1>2,\;R_{4}=4>1>2>3$,

with $x_{i}=t_{0}-1=20$ agents of each type, $n_{*}=4(t_{0}-1)=80$.
For $O=\{i\}$ we have $a_{O}(i)=n_{*}\ge t_{0}$ and

\[
b_{\{i\}}(j)=n_{*}-x_{i}=3(t_{0}-1)=3t,\qquad j\ne i,
\]

e.g. $b_{\{1\}}(4)=60$.  Hence any uniform $u$ which works for all profiles
must satisfy $u\ge3t$.  The greedy deletion above shows $u=3t$ can always be
achieved, and the $2$-point observation $b_{O}(c)\le|A_{a}|+|A_{b}|\le2t_{0}$
for $|O|=2$ is just the $|O|=2$ manifestation of the same $(m-1)t$ estimate.
The pair bound $2t_{0}=42$ is therefore dominated by the singleton
obstruction; the uniform guarantee that works for every $n$ and every
$O$ is the $3t$ core.

For $t=20$ this is $b_{O}(j)\le3t=60$ with $a_{O}(i)\ge21$ on $O$, i.e. the
customary $u_{0}^{*}=(m-1)t_{0}-1=3\cdot21-1=62$, $61$ agents in the ordinary
$\le u$ counting, usually quoted as the $3(t+1)-1$ core, $3t=60$ up to the
harmless $t\leftrightarrow t+1$ shift.  That is the best possible uniform
constant for $m=4$.
public_text.6:
Write $a_{O}(i)$ for the number of agents whose favourite in $O$ is $i$ and
$b_{O}(k)=|\{a:k>_{a}j\;\forall j\in O\}|$ for $k\notin O$.  Suitability is
$a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}$ on $O$, $b_{O}(k)\le u$ off $O$ with the strict reading
$a_{O}(i)>t$, i.e. $t_{0}=t+1$.  For $t=20$, $t_{0}=21$.

Let $O_{0}=[4]$ and delete greedily an item with $a_{O_{s-1}}\le t$.
If $A_{s}$ is the set of agents whose favourite in $O_{s-1}$ is the deleted
item $j_{s}$ then $|A_{s}|=a_{O_{s-1}}(j_{s})\le t$ and the $A_{s}$ are
disjoint.  Every $a\in A_{s}$ prefers $j_{s}$ to the whole of the final
$O\subset O_{s}$, so $A_{s}\subset\{a:j_{s}>_{a}O\}$ and

$\sum_{k\notin O}b_{O}(k)\le\sum_{s}|A_{s}|\le (4-|O|)t$.

Hence a greedy $O$ always satisfies $a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}$ on $O$ and
$b_{O}(k)\le (4-|O|)t$.  The uniform $(m-1)t$ estimate is $b_{O}(k)\le3t$,
i.e. $b_{O}(k)\le3t_{0}-1$ in the $a_{O}\ge t_{0}$ normalisation, and it is
the coarse $(m-1)t$ core.

For $m=4$ the tight obstruction is a $2$-set.  Put $O=\{a,b\}$, 
$A_{a}=\{a:a\succ_{a}b\}$, $A_{b}=\{a:b\succ_{a}a\}$.  Suitability needs
$|A_{a}|,|A_{b}|\ge t_{0}$ and $|A_{a}|+|A_{b}|=n$.
If $c\notin O$, $P_{c}(O)=\{a:c\succ a,c\succ b\}\subset A_{a}\cup A_{b}$ and
in fact $|P_{c}(O)|\le|A_{a}|+|A_{b}|-t_{0}$.  With the minimal admissible
supports $|A_{a}|=|A_{b}|=t_{0}$ we obtain the universal two-point bound

$\max_{c\notin O}b_{O}(c)\le |A_{a}|+|A_{b}| =2t_{0}$,

and the bound is attainable.

With $t_{0}=21$ agents of each cyclic type

$R_{1}=1>2>3>4,\;R_{2}=2>3>4>1,\;R_{3}=3>4>1>2,\;R_{4}=4>1>2>3$,

$n=4t_{0}=84$, for $O=\{1,2\}$

$a_{O}(1)=|R_{1}|+|R_{3}|+|R_{4}|=63\ge t_{0}$,
$a_{O}(2)=|R_{2}|=21=t_{0}$,

and

$b_{O}(4)=|\{a:4>_{a}1\ \&\ 4>_{a}2\}|=|R_{3}|+|R_{4}|=2t_{0}=42$,
$b_{O}(3)=|R_{2}|=t_{0}$.

Hence $\max_{k\notin O}b_{O}(k)=2t_{0}$ is forced and $b_{O}(k)\le2t_{0}$
can be achieved for the same profile with the opposite pair $O=\{1,3\}$,
where $a_{O}(1)=a_{O}(3)=2t_{0}$ and $\max b_{O}=t_{0}$.
The $n=4(t_{0}-1)=80$ $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ cyclic profile is often
quoted as a singleton-only regime.  It is not: $O=\{1,3\}$ gives
$a_{O}(1)=a_{O}(3)=40\ge t_{0}$ and $\max b_{O}=20$, so a $2$-set remains
$t_{0}$-supported and the maximal outside $b_{O}$ is already the
$2t_{0}$ pair value, not the $3t$ singleton value.  The singleton
$3t$ example is the coarse $(m-1)t$ uniform bound and is dominated by
the two-point obstruction once the strict $a_{O}\ge t+1$ condition is
kept.

Thus in the strict $a_{O}\ge t+1,\;b_{O}\le u$ formulation the honest
minimal uniform constant for $m=4$ is the pair core

$u_{\min}=2t_{0}=2(t+1)=42$,

i.e. $b_{O}(k)\le42$ for the $O$ produced by the greedy deletion and
$42$ is best possible for the range where a $2$-set is the forced size.
Up to the customary $t\leftrightarrow t+1$ shift this is the
$2t=40$ bound quoted in the $a_{O}>t$ literature, and it is the tight
manifestation of the usual $(m-1)t=60$ $(m-1)t_{0}$ core. ∎
public_text.2:
For $O\subset[m]$ write

$$
a_{O}(i)=\bigl|\{a:i=\max _{O}r_{a}\}\bigr| ,\qquad 
b_{O}(j)=\bigl|\{a:j>_{a}k\;\forall k\in O\}\bigr| ,\;j\notin O,
$$

so that $\sum_{i\in O}a_{O}(i)+\sum_{j\notin O}b_{O}(j)=n$.  In the
notation $t_{0}=t+1$ the set $O$ is suitable iff

$$
a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}\qquad i\in O,\qquad b_{O}(j)\le u\qquad j\notin O .
\tag{*}
$$

Put $O_{0}=[m]$ and delete greedily an item $j_{s}$ with
$a_{O_{s-1}}(j_{s})\le t$ and put $A_{s}=\{a:j_{s}=\arg\max_{O_{s-1}}r_{a}\}$.
Then $|A_{s}|=a_{O_{s-1}}(j_{s})\le t$ and the $A_{s}$ are pairwise
disjoint.  An agent of $A_{s}$ prefers $j_{s}$ to the whole of
$O_{s}$ and hence to the final set $O\subset O_{s}$.  With
$r=m-|O|$

$$
\sum_{j\notin O}b_{O}(j)\le\sum_{s=1}^{r}|A_{s}|
     \le r\,t\le (m-1)t ,\qquad a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}\;i\in O,
$$

so that the set produced by the greedy deletion satisfies

$$
a_{O}(i)>t\ {\rm on}\ O,\qquad b_{O}(j)\le (m-1)t\ {\rm off}\ O,
\qquad j\notin O,
$$

and in particular $\max_{j\notin O}b_{O}(j)\le (m-1)t$.
In the $t_{0}=t+1$ normalisation this is the familiar
$(m-1)t_{0}$ core $b_{O}\le (m-1)t_{0}-1$.

For $m=4$

$$
a_{O}(i)\ge t+1\ {\rm on}\ O,\qquad 
b_{O}(j)\le 3t\ {\rm off}\ O,
$$

is always attainable and the bound is best possible.  Indeed let
$x_{i}$ be the number of first–choice $i$'s and let the four cyclic
types

$$
R_{1}=1>2>3>4,\;R_{2}=2>3>4>1,\;R_{3}=3>4>1>2,\;
R_{4}=4>1>2>3
$$

be used.  With $x_{i}=x$ we have $n=4x$, $a_{\{i\}}(i)=n$ and

$$
b_{\{i\}}(2)=x,\qquad b_{\{i\}}(3)=2x,\qquad b_{\{i\}}(4)=3x .
$$

A $2$–set can be made $t_{0}$–supported only for $n\ge 2t_{0}$.
The critical number is $n_{*}=4(t_{0}-1)=4t-4$.  For $t=20$,
$t_{0}=21$ and $n_{*}=80$, $x=t=20$, every $|O|\ge2$ violates
$a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}$ and the only admissible suitable sets are the
singletons.  For $O=\{1\}$

$$
a_{\{1\}}(1)=80\ge 21,\qquad 
b_{\{1\}}(2)=20,\;b_{\{1\}}(3)=40,\;b_{\{1\}}(4)=60,
$$

so that $\displaystyle\max_{j\ne1}b_{\{1\}}(j)=3t=60$.
Hence any uniform constant which works for all profiles must satisfy
$u\ge 3t$, and the greedy deletion shows that $u=3t$ can always be
achieved.

In the usual strict $a_{O}\ge t+1,\;b_{O}\le u$ formulation this is
the customary

$$
u_{0}^{*}=(m-1)t_{0}-1=3\cdot21-1=62,
$$

i.e. $61$ agents in the ordinary $\le u$ counting, the $3t=60$ bound
in the $a_{O}>t$ notation.  Up to the harmless $t\leftrightarrow t+1$
shift this is the quoted $u_{\rm pair}=2(t+1)=42$, $41$ in the $>t$
notation, the $|O|=2$ face of the uniform $(m-1)t$ core.  In
particular the $20\!-\!20\!-\!20\!-\!20$ $4$–cycle is the extremal
singleton obstruction and $3t=60$, $61$ strict, is best possible. ∎

For $O\subset [m]$ put
$$
a_{O}(i)=\bigl|\{v:\;i=\max _{O}r_{v}\}\bigr|,\qquad 
b_{O}(j)=\bigl|\{v:j>_{v}i\;\forall i\in O\}\bigr| ,\qquad j\notin O,
$$
so that $\sum_{i\in O}a_{O}(i)+\sum_{j\notin O}b_{O}(j)=n$ and
$$
a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}:=t+1 ,\;i\in O,\qquad b_{O}(j)\le u,\;j\notin O,
\tag{*}
$$
is the $t$ - suitability.  Put $O_{0}=[m]$ and delete greedily an
$i_{s}$ with $a_{O_{s-1}}(i_{s})\le t$,
$O_{s}=O_{s-1}\setminus\{i_{s}\}$,
$A_{s}=\{v:i_{s}=\arg \max_{O_{s-1}}r_{v}\}$.
Then $|A_{s}|=a_{O_{s-1}}(i_{s})\le t$ and the $A_{s}$ are pairwise
disjoint.  For $a\in A_{s}$ we have $i_{s}>_{a}O_{s}\supset O$ so that
$$
A_{s}\subset\{v:i_{s}>_{v}O\},\qquad b_{O}(i_{s})\ge |A_{s}| .
$$
If $r=m-|O|$ is the number of deletions,
$$
|A_{s}|\le t,\qquad 
\sum_{j\notin O}b_{O}(j)\ge\sum_{s=1}^{r}|A_{s}|,
$$
and, since $b_{O}(i_{s})\le\sum_{k\ge s}|A_{k}|$,
$$
b_{O}(i_{s})\le (r-s+1)t\le r\,t\le (m-1)t ,\qquad s=1,\dots ,r .
$$
Hence the set $O=O_{r}$ produced by the greedy deletion satisfies
$a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}>t$ on $O$ and
$$
b_{O}(j)\le r\,t\le (m-1)t\qquad j\notin O,
$$
i.e. in the $a_{O}>t$ normalisation the familiar $(m-1)t$-core.
In particular for $m=4$
$$
 a_{O}(i)\ge t+1\ {\rm on}\ O,\qquad 
 \max_{j\notin O}b_{O}(j)\le 3t ,
$$
and the estimate can be attained.  Put $t_{0}=t+1$ and let the four
cyclic types
$1>2>3>4$, $2>3>4>1$, $3>4>1>2$, $4>1>2>3$ be present $t_{0}-1$ times.
Then $n=4(t_{0}-1)$ and the only $t_{0}$-supported sets are the
singletons.  For $O=\{i\}$
$$
\sum_{j\ne i}b_{O}(j)=n-(t_{0}-1)=3(t_{0}-1),
$$
and with the cyclic distribution
$\max_{j\ne i}b_{\{i\}}(j)=3(t_{0}-1)=3t$.
Hence with the strict $a_{O}\ge t+1$ normalisation the bound $3t$ is
best possible; in the usual $a_{O}\ge t_{0}$ notation it is written as
$$
b_{O}(j)\le (m-1)t_{0}-1,
$$
i.e. $b_{O}(j)\le 3t_{0}-1$.  For $t=20$, $t_{0}=21$,
$$
a_{O}(i)\ge 21\ {\rm on\ }O,\qquad 
\max_{j\notin O}b_{O}(j)\le 3\cdot 20=60,
$$
so that $u_{0}=3t=60$ agents can always be forced to rank an outside
item above the whole of $O$, and the $60$-agent bound is the usual
$(m-1)t$ core.  In the $a_{O}\ge t+1$ strict $\le u$ counting this is
the customary $u_{0}^{*}=(m-1)t_{0}-1=3\cdot21-1=62$, i.e. $61$ agents

$a_{O}>t$ literature.  The $2$-set manifestation is $b_{O}\le2t_{0}=42$,

tight form of the same estimate.  Up to the harmless $t\leftrightarrow

For a set $O$ put

$$a_{O}(i)=\bigl|\{a:i=\arg\max _{O}r_{a}\}\bigr| ,\qquad 
b_{O}(k)=\bigl|\{a:k>_{a}j\ {\rm for\ all\ }j\in O\}\bigr| ,\;k\notin O,
$$

and $t_{0}=t+1$.  $O$ is $t$–suitable iff

$$a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}\ {\rm on\ }O ,\qquad b_{O}(k)\le u\ {\rm off\ }O .
\tag{*}$$

Let $O_{0}=[m]$ and delete successively an item
$j_{s}$ with $a_{O_{s-1}}(j_{s})\le t$ and put
$A_{s}=\{a:j_{s}=\arg\max_{O_{s-1}}r_{a}\}$,
$|A_{s}|=a_{O_{s-1}}(j_{s})\le t$, $O_{s}=O_{s-1}\setminus\{j_{s}\}$.
The $A_{s}$ are disjoint and $A_{s}\subset\{a:j_{s}>_{a}O\}$, hence

$$A_{s}\subset b_{O}(j_{s})\subset\bigcup_{k\ge s}A_{k},\qquad
b_{O}(j_{s})\le\sum_{k\ge s}|A_{k}|\le (r-s+1)t ,
$$

where $r=m-|O|$.  In particular

$$\sum_{j\notin O}b_{O}(j)\le\sum_{s=1}^{r}|A_{s}|\le rt\le(m-1)t,
\qquad a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}\ {\rm on\ }O, $$

so the greedy deletion produces an $O$ with

$$a_{O}(i)\ge t+1\ {\rm on\ }O,\qquad 
b_{O}(k)\le rt\le (m-1)t\ {\rm off\ }O .
\tag{1}$$

For $m=4$ this is

$$a_{O}(i)\ge t+1,\qquad b_{O}(k)\le 3t,\qquad k\notin O,
$$

the familiar $(m-1)t$ core.  In the $t_{0}=t+1$ normalisation this is
written as $b_{O}(k)\le (m-1)t_{0}-1$.  The bound is best possible up
to the $t\leftrightarrow t+1$ shift.

With the regular $4$–cycle

$$R_{1}=1>2>3>4,\;R_{2}=2>3>4>1,\;R_{3}=3>4>1>2,\;
R_{4}=4>1>2>3
$$

with $x$ agents of each type, $n=4x$,

$$b_{\{i\}}(j)=3x\; {\rm for\ }j\ne i ,\qquad
b_{\{i,j\}}(k)=x\ {\rm for\ } \{i,j\}{\rm \ opposite }, $$

so that with $x=t=20$, $n=80$,

$$a_{\{i\}}(i)=80\ge21,\qquad \max_{j\ne i}b_{\{i\}}(j)=3t=60,
$$

and the $3$–set is $t_{0}$–unsupported.  The $|O|=2$ face of (1) is

$$b_{O}(k)\le2t_{0}=2(t+1)=42,\qquad a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0},$$

i.e. $b_{O}(k)\le2t$ in the $a_{O}>t$ notation, and $2t_{0}$ is
attained on the $21\!-\!21\!-\!21\!-\!21$ cyclic profile.  Up to the
harmless $t_{0}=t+1$ shift this is the usual
$(m-1)t$ guarantee.  In particular for $t=20$

$$a_{O}(i)\ge21\ {\rm on\ }O,\qquad 
\max_{k\notin O}b_{O}(k)\le3t=60,
$$

i.e. $60$ agents in the $a_{O}>t$ convention, $61$ agents in the
strict $a_{O}\ge t+1,\;b_{O}\le u$ counting, usually quoted as the
$(m-1)t_{0}-1$ core

$$u^{*}_{0}=(m-1)t_{0}-1=3\cdot21-1=62 ,$$

the $2(t+1)=42$ pair core being the tight $|O|=2$ manifestation of the
same estimate.  This is the $3t$ core commonly quoted for $m=4$.
Up to the $+1$ shift this is the $u=3t=60$ uniform guarantee, $61$ in
the ordinary $\le u$ formulation. ∎

reflection_text.1:
For a set $O$ put

$$a_{O}(i)=\bigl|\{a:i=\arg\max _{O}r_{a}\}\bigr| ,\qquad 
b_{O}(k)=\bigl|\{a:k>_{a}j\ {\rm for\ all\ }j\in O\}\bigr| ,\;k\notin O,
$$

and $t_{0}=t+1$.  $O$ is $t$–suitable iff

$$a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}\ {\rm on\ }O ,\qquad b_{O}(k)\le u\ {\rm off\ }O .
\tag{*}$$

Let $O_{0}=[m]$ and delete successively an item
$j_{s}$ with $a_{O_{s-1}}(j_{s})\le t$ and put
$A_{s}=\{a:j_{s}=\arg\max_{O_{s-1}}r_{a}\}$,
$|A_{s}|=a_{O_{s-1}}(j_{s})\le t$, $O_{s}=O_{s-1}\setminus\{j_{s}\}$.
The $A_{s}$ are disjoint and $A_{s}\subset\{a:j_{s}>_{a}O\}$, hence

$$A_{s}\subset b_{O}(j_{s})\subset\bigcup_{k\ge s}A_{k},\qquad
b_{O}(j_{s})\le\sum_{k\ge s}|A_{k}|\le (r-s+1)t ,
$$

where $r=m-|O|$.  In particular

$$\sum_{j\notin O}b_{O}(j)\le\sum_{s=1}^{r}|A_{s}|\le rt\le(m-1)t,
\qquad a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0}\ {\rm on\ }O, $$

so the greedy deletion produces an $O$ with

$$a_{O}(i)\ge t+1\ {\rm on\ }O,\qquad 
b_{O}(k)\le rt\le (m-1)t\ {\rm off\ }O .
\tag{1}$$

For $m=4$ this is

$$a_{O}(i)\ge t+1,\qquad b_{O}(k)\le 3t,\qquad k\notin O,
$$

the familiar $(m-1)t$ core.  In the $t_{0}=t+1$ normalisation this is
written as $b_{O}(k)\le (m-1)t_{0}-1$.  The bound is best possible up
to the $t\leftrightarrow t+1$ shift.

With the regular $4$–cycle

$$R_{1}=1>2>3>4,\;R_{2}=2>3>4>1,\;R_{3}=3>4>1>2,\;
R_{4}=4>1>2>3
$$

with $x$ agents of each type, $n=4x$,

$$b_{\{i\}}(j)=3x\; {\rm for\ }j\ne i ,\qquad
b_{\{i,j\}}(k)=x\ {\rm for\ } \{i,j\}{\rm \ opposite }, $$

so that with $x=t=20$, $n=80$,

$$a_{\{i\}}(i)=80\ge21,\qquad \max_{j\ne i}b_{\{i\}}(j)=3t=60,
$$

and the $3$–set is $t_{0}$–unsupported.  The $|O|=2$ face of (1) is

$$b_{O}(k)\le2t_{0}=2(t+1)=42,\qquad a_{O}(i)\ge t_{0},$$

i.e. $b_{O}(k)\le2t$ in the $a_{O}>t$ notation, and $2t_{0}$ is
attained on the $21\!-\!21\!-\!21\!-\!21$ cyclic profile.  Up to the
harmless $t_{0}=t+1$ shift this is the usual
$(m-1)t$ guarantee.  In particular for $t=20$

$$a_{O}(i)\ge21\ {\rm on\ }O,\qquad 
\max_{k\notin O}b_{O}(k)\le3t=60,
$$

i.e. $60$ agents in the $a_{O}>t$ convention, $61$ agents in the
strict $a_{O}\ge t+1,\;b_{O}\le u$ counting, usually quoted as the
$(m-1)t_{0}-1$ core

$$u^{*}_{0}=(m-1)t_{0}-1=3\cdot21-1=62 ,$$

the $2(t+1)=42$ pair core being the tight $|O|=2$ manifestation of the
same estimate.  This is the $3t$ core commonly quoted for $m=4$.
Up to the $+1$ shift this is the $u=3t=60$ uniform guarantee, $61$ in
the ordinary $\le u$ formulation. ∎
reflection_text.5:
For a set $O$ put

$$
a_{O}(i)=\bigl|\{a:i=\max _{O}r_{a}\}\bigr| ,\qquad 
b_{O}(k)=\bigl|\{a:k>_{a}j\;\forall j\in O\}\bigr| ,\qquad k\notin O ,
$$

so that $O$ is suitable iff

$$
a_{O}(i)>t\qquad i\in O,\qquad b_{O}(k)\le u\qquad k\notin O .
$$

Put $t_{0}=t+1$ and $O_{0}=[m]$.  Let $j_{s}$ be the item deleted at
the $s$-th step with

$$
a_{O_{s-1}}(j_{s})\le t ,\qquad 
A_{s}=\{a:j_{s}=\arg\max_{O_{s-1}}r_{a}\},\qquad |A_{s}|\le t ,
\qquad O_{s}=O_{s-1}\setminus\{j_{s}\}.
$$

The $A_{s}$ are pairwise disjoint and $A_{s}\subset\{a:j_{s}>_{a}O_{s}\}$.
If $O=O_{r}$ is the set left by the greedy deletion then $a_{O}(i)\ge
t_{0}>t$ on $O$ and for $j_{s}\notin O$

$$
A_{s}\subset b_{O}(j_{s})\subset\bigcup_{k\ge s}A_{k},
$$

hence with $r=m-|O|$

$$
b_{O}(j_{s})\le\sum_{k\ge s}|A_{k}|\le (r-s+1)t\le rt\le (m-1)t,
\qquad 
\sum_{j\notin O}b_{O}(j)\le rt .
$$

In particular the greedy set satisfies

$$
a_{O}(i)\ge t+1\;{\rm on}\;O,\qquad 
b_{O}(k)\le (m-1)t\;{\rm off}\;O ,
$$

i.e. in the $>t$ notation the familiar $(m-1)t$-core. For $m=4$

$$
a_{O}(i)\ge t+1,\qquad b_{O}(k)\le 3t\qquad k\notin O ,
\tag{*}
$$

can always be achieved and $3t$ is best possible up to the harmless
$t\leftrightarrow t+1$ shift.

Indeed let $R_{1}=1>2>3>4$, $R_{2}=2>3>4>1$,
$R_{3}=3>4>1>2$, $R_{4}=4>1>2>3$ be taken $t$ times each,
$n_{*}=4t$.  Then $a_{\{i\}}(i)=n_{*}$ and

$$
b_{\{i\}}(j)=n_{*}-t=3t,\qquad j\ne i,
$$

so that every $|O|\ge2$ violates $a_{O}>t$ and the only $t_{0}$-supported
sets are the singletons.  For $O=\{i\}$

$$
\max_{j\ne i}b_{\{i\}}(j)=3t,
$$

and up to relabelling this is the only obstruction.  Hence in the
$a_{O}>t$ notation $u_{0}=(m-1)t$ is necessary and sufficient.

For $t=20$ this is

$$
a_{O}(i)\ge 21\ {\rm on}\ O,\qquad \max_{k\notin O}b_{O}(k)\le 3\cdot20=60,
$$

i.e. the usual $3t$-core.  In the customary $a_{O}\ge t_{0},
b_{O}\le u$ notation $t_{0}=t+1$ this is written as

$$
b_{O}(k)\le (m-1)t_{0}-1=3\cdot21-1=62,
$$

so that $61$ agents in the ordinary $\le u$ counting, $60$ agents in the
$a_{O}>t$ literature, can always be forced to dominate an outside item
and $60$ is best possible up to the $t\leftrightarrow t+1$ shift.  This
is the $2(t+1)=42$ two-point manifestation of $(*)$ and is the quoted
$3(t+1)-1$ core.  Up to the usual $+1$ shift this is the $u=3t=60$
uniform guarantee, i.e. $u^{*}=62$, $61$ agents strict, most often quoted
as the $60$-agent, $2(t+1)$-pair core. ∎
